body:
**Credit name.** Mohsen Karimi (ORCID 0009-0004-1055-8267)

**Claim.** 683 improved upper bounds for s(n), n in [1184, 3775]; in 85 cases the previous entry was the trivial grid ⌈√n⌉. Each is a valid non-overlapping packing of n unit squares in a square of the stated side, with an exact rational certificate.

**Construction.** In a box of side S just below an integer K, two strips of squares tilted by a small angle are attached to the walls (rows on the bottom wall, columns on the right wall); the rest is an axis-parallel grid. Consecutive rows in a strip touch (vertical pitch cos a, shift sin a), so a strip of m rows gains one square per grid column when m(1 − cos a) ≥ sin a + (K − S). All angles have rational tan(a/2).

**Verification.** Certificates (`n S` header, then `x y t`, t = tan(θ/2), exact rationals) pass the exact verifier `verify_bound_certificate.py` of Mishapolk/square-packing-records (VALID).

**Data.** https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23624433 — table of new vs previous sides and `regenerate.py`, which rebuilds every certificate exactly. Also registered at Mishapolk/square-packing-records.

| n | previous best | new side |
|---|---|---|
| 1813 | 43.000000 | 42.992495 |
| 1987 | 45.000000 | 44.985304 |
| 2342 | 48.988287 | 48.900000 |

The code was written with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic) under my direction.
**Credit name.** Mohsen Karimi, independent researcher, Zanjan, Iran (ORCID 0009-0004-1055-8267).

**Claim.** 683 improved upper bounds for s(n), for n between 1184 and 3775. In 85 of these cases the best previous entry was the trivial grid ⌈√n⌉; in the others it was a non-trivial record from Mishapolk/square-packing-records (commit 7e82c64, 23 Oct 2026) or franciscouzo/square-packing (24 Oct 2026). Examples (previous → new): n=1813: 43 → 42.992495; n=1987: 45 → 44.985304; n=2342: 48.988287 → 48.9; n=1184: 34.909679 → 34.908235. Full list with previous and new sides in records.csv.

**Certificate.** Exact rational certificates (header `n S`, then `x y t` per square, t = tan(θ/2)), pinned at Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23624433 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23624433). The record holds records.csv with every parameter and regenerate.py, which rebuilds all 683 certificates exactly (plain Python 3, about 10 s).

**Checking.** Every certificate was accepted by `verify_bound_certificate.py` of Mishapolk/square-packing-records: exact rational arithmetic, separating-axis test, result VALID (closed container). Rerun: `python3 regenerate.py` then `python3 check_packing.py certificates/n<N>.cert` from that repository.

**What the checkers share.** One checker (Polkovskyi's exact verifier); the construction code is mine. No independent second checker yet.

**Not done.** No independent second verifier; no lower bounds; sides are near-minimal for this construction family but not optimised further.

**Lineage and credit.** New construction: in a box of side S just below an integer K, two strips of squares tilted by a small angle are attached to the walls (rows on the bottom wall, columns on the right wall); the rest is an axis-parallel grid. Consecutive rows in a strip touch (vertical pitch cos a, horizontal shift sin a), so a strip of m rows gains one square per grid column when m(1 − cos a) ≥ sin a + (K − S). Angles have rational tan(a/2). Also registered at Mishapolk/square-packing-records issue #1. Credit to Mohsen Karimi.

**AI assistance.** The idea (low-angle strips attached to the walls, with a cost–benefit choice of strip size and angle) is mine. Claude (Anthropic) wrote and ran the code for the search, the exact certificates and the verification, under my direction.

comments.body: Full details in the format of the result-registration template:

Related theorem (preprint, Mohsen Karimi): for every integer K ≥ 16, s(n) < K whenever n ≤ K² − 8√K − 19; equivalently W(s) ≤ 8√K + 19 for s in [K − 1/K, K). This improves the exponent from 3/5 (Bui; McClenagan) to 1/2 for sides just below an integer. Proof by the same two-strip construction: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23627827

Update (version 2): the same construction now gives 2824 improved upper bounds for n between 1184 and 9944 (867 of them over the trivial grid ⌈√n⌉), all with exact rational certificates that pass the exact verifier of Mishapolk/square-packing-records. Data and regenerate.py: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23624432 (all versions; the latest version holds all 2824 records).
